name: Road Knot-Charms

rarity.note: Hedge-craft: weak, real about half the time, and priced accordingly.

summary: Knotted cords sold at every caravan-master's tent: a knot for safe crossing, a knot for dry feet, a knot against bad company. Tied by Road-Singers and caravan grandmothers using hedge-craft — a spoken bargain with the echo, coaxed into cord. Most do nothing. Some work exactly once. Nobody can tell which until it matters.
origin: As old as roads; the current styles date to the Salt Roads era (~300 AA)
current_whereabouts: Every road, wrist, and saddle-pack on Aurelith.
properties: A working knot unties itself at the moment of its purpose — that's how you know it was real
Placebo knots stay tied forever, which their owners find reassuring anyway
Cutting another traveler's knot uninvited is road-code's pettiest capital offense
keepers: Everyone; the Road-Singers' grandmothers hold the genuinely reliable patterns.
value_or_danger: A bit each. The one that works is worth whatever it saves.
adventure_hooks: A player's crossing-knot unties at the exact moment an ambush springs — someone paid for a working charm on their behalf. Who?
A grandmother offers to tie 'the old knot' whose purpose she will not name; the price is a true story told to her fire.
